name: Snap-Fit Calculator
blurb: insertion force and strain of a cantilever snap hook
intro: The strain at the root of a rectangular cantilever snap hook and the force to push it home and pull it apart, from the Bayer snap-fit design guide's cantilever equations. Material strain limits, moduli and friction are typical values.

inputs.label: Arm shape
options: Tapered to half thickness at the hook

inputs.label: Arm length
inputs.help: From the root to the hook's contact point.

inputs.label: Retaining angle
inputs.help: 90° is a square hook that does not come apart.

inputs.label: Friction coefficient
inputs.help: Leave empty for the material's value against steel.

inputs.label: Assembled and taken apart often
inputs.help: Uses 60 % of the single-assembly strain limit.

examples.title: ABS lid clip, 15 mm arm, 1 mm undercut

usage: Give the material, arm shape, arm length, root thickness, width and deflection (undercut depth) in mm, and the lead-in and retaining angles in degrees. It returns the root strain in % against the material's limit, the allowed deflection in mm, and the deflection, insertion and separation forces in N. Use it when sizing a snap hook on a plastic enclosure.
sources: Bayer MaterialScience, Snap-Fit Joints for Plastics - A Design Guide: cantilever equations, permissible strains and friction coefficients
Material data: typical values, check the grade datasheet
